Vote against Iran on Nuclear issue 
*83. SHRIAMAR SINGH: 
SHRIABUASIMAZMI: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the statement of the 
U.S. Ambassador to India to the effect that if India did not vote against Iran 
on nuclear issue at the International Atomic Energy Agency, the fall out on July 
18, 2005 deal would be devastating and the initiative would die; and 
(b) if so, Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHRI ANAND SHARMA): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The 
Government's attention was drawn to an interview given by US Ambassador 
David Mulford on January 25, 2006 in which he said that if India decided not to 
vote with US and EU 3 on the Iran nuclear issue, its effect on the civil nuclear 
cooperation initiative would be "devastating" and that the US Congress would 
"simply stop considering the matter". 
The Government responded on January 25 itself by issuing a statement 
that India's position on the Iran nuclear issue at the IAEA will be based on 
India's own independent judgement and national interests. The Government 
categorically rejected any attempt to link this to the proposed India-US 
agreement on civil nuclear energy cooperation, which stood on its own merits. 
Foreign Secretary called in the US Ambassador on January 26, 2006 to convey 
to him that the remarks made by him "were inappropriate and not conducive 
to building a strong partnership between OUT two independent democracies". 
Foreign Secretary informed the US Ambassador that India's vote on any 
possible resolution on the Iran nuclear issue at the IAEA would be 
determined by India's own 
9 

RAJYA SABHA [23 February, 2006] 
judgement of the merits of the case. Concerning the proposed India-US civil 
nuclear energy cooperation agreement, the Foreign Secretary reaffirmed 
India's stand that both countries needed to work in the spirit of the 18 July, 2005 
Joint Statement and in strict conformity with the reciprocal commitments contained 
therein. The Ambassador expressed his sincere regrets, saying that his remarks 
had been taken out of context, and that it was not his intention at all to question 
India's right to take decisions on the basis of its own national interests.

Kuala Lumpur Declaration on the East Asia Summit 
WE, the Heads of State/Government of the Member Countries of the 
Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), Australia, People's Republic 
of China, Republic of India, Japan, Republic of Korea and New Zealand, on the 
occasion of the historic First East Asia Summit on 14 December 2005 in Kuala 
Lumpur, Malaysia; RECALLING the decision of the 10th ASEAN Summit and 
supported by the 8th ASEAN Plus Three Summit held on 29 November 2004 in 
Vientiane, Lao PDR, to convene the First East Asia Summit in Malaysia in 
2005; 
REITERATING our commitment to the purposes and principles of the 
Charter of the United Nations, the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation in Southeast 
Asia and other recognised principles of international law; 
ACKNOWLEDGING that in a rapidly changing international 
environment, our economies and societies have become increasingly 
interlinked and interdependent; 
REALISING the increasing range of challenges fating the world and 
the need for concerted regional and global efforts to respond to these challenges; 
RECOGNISING our shared interests in ac hieving peace, security and 
prosperity in East Asia and the world at large; 
DESIROUS of creating a peaceful envir onment by further enhancing 
cooperation and strengthening the ex isting bounds of friendship among our 
countries in keeping with the principles of equality, partnership, consultation 
and consensus thereby contributing to peace, security and economic prosperity 
in the region and the world at large; 
CONVINCED of the importance of strengthening bilateral and 
multilateral interactions and cooperation among the participating countries of the 
East Asia Summit and the world at large on issues of common interest and 
concern in order to enhance peace and economic prosperity; 
REITERATING the conviction that the effective functioning of 
multiateral systems will continue to be indispensable for advancing 
economic development; 
RECOGNISING that this region is today a source of dynamism for the 
world economy;

DO HEREBY DECLARE: 
FIRST, that we have established the East Asia Summit as a forum for dialogue on 
broad strategic, political and economic issues of common interest and concern with the 
aim of promoting peace, stability and economic prosperity in East Asia.

building in this region will be consistent with and reinforce the realization of the ASEAN

recognised values with ASEAN as the driving force working in partnership with the other

Tsunami warning centre in Hyderabad 
456. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Will the Minister of OCEAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the present status of the establishment of Tsunami warning centre in 
Hyderabad; 
(b) whether Government are confident that it would give the exact 
prediction of Tsunami; 
(c) if so, the details therefor; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF OCEAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): 
(a) to (d) Department is setting up an Early Warning System for Tsunami and 
Storm Surges in the Indian Ocean Region with the following components: 
• installation of Tsunami warnin g sensors close to the ocean 
bottom at appropriate locales in the Indian Ocean, with real time 
connectivity; 
• Tide gauge and data buoys networking to validate arrival of 
Tsunami waves at the coast; 
• strengthening of the existing seismological network to indicate, near 
real time occurrence of tsunamigenic earthquakes; 
• Modelling of the inundation scenarios for the entire coast and 
mapping of potential risk areas; 
• collection of information, analysis and generating status 
advisories. 
The warning system is scheduled to be operational by September, 2007. A 
centre would be set up at Indian Na tional Centre for Ocean Information 
Services (INCOIS), Hyderabad on a 24x7 basis. 
Currently 11 tide gauges have been installed along the coastal areas of the 
country and connected th rough Global System for Mobile Communications 
(GSM) for real time communication to National Institute of Ocean Technology 
(NIOT) and in turn automated data delivery to INCOIS Hyderabad. NIOT has 
processed procurement of bottom pressure recorders which will detect tsunami 
waves in the deep sea. 
79

The detection of Tsunami waves through Bottom Pressure Recorders and 
tide gauges are the reliable methods.

Per capita power in Bihar 
† 478. SHRI MANGANI LAL MANDAL: Will the Minister of POWER 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that per capita power generation and 
consumption in Bihar is less than all other States of the country; and 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the solution thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) and 
(b) Yes, Sir. The per capita power generation and consumption in the State of 
Bihar is among the lowest in the country mainly due to lack of investment in 
the power generation and distribution segments. At present, in the State Sector, a 
meager generation capacity aggregating about 644 MW only exists, which is not 
sufficient to meet the electricity requirements of the State. There has been no 
capacity addition over a decade now in the State Sector or private sector. The 
Plant Load Factor of Bihar State Elect ricity Board is also lowest in the

490. SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state:

generation, transmission and distribution of electricity? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) 
Prior to enactment of the Electricity Act 2003, various States had enacted State 
Electricity Reforms Acts which provided for reorganization of their State 
Electricity Boards (SEB). The Electricity Act, 2003 provides for the 
reorganization of the State Electricity Boards. Section 172(a) of the Act provides 
that the State Electricity Boards (SEB ) shall be deemed to be the State 
Transmission Utility (STU) and a licensee under the provisions of the Act for a 
period of one year from the appointed date, i.e. 10th June, 2003. This section 
further provides that the State Government may, by notification, authorize the SEB to 
continue to function as the STU or a licensee for such further period beyond the 
stipulated period of one year, as may be mutually decided by the Central 
Government and the State Government. 
(b) So far, 12 States have reorganized their SEBs. Orissa, Haryana, Andhra 
Pradesh, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Uttaranchal, Rajasthan, Delhi, Gujarat and 
Madhya Pradesh have done so under their State Electricity Reforms Acts. Assam 
and Maharashtra have reorganized their SEBs under the provisions of the Electricity 
Act, 2003. The SEBs of Madhya Pradesh and Assam presently continue to do 
the licensee function of trading of electricity only, under section 172(a) of the 
Act 
(c) The Government has launched following major initiatives to improve the 
generation, transmission and distribution of electricity and to make power 
sector competitive and viable: 
(i) Accelerating capacity addition to eliminate shortages. 
(ii) Launching of Ultra Mega projects through tariff based competitive 
bidding. 
(iii) Partnership for excellence progamme for improving operation and 
maintenance practices and renovation and modernisation for 
improving Plant Load Factor (PLF) of poorly performing thermal 
power stations in the Country.

(APDRP) for assisting States in investment in sub-transmission

vStringent legal provisions relating to theft of electricity. 
(vti) Completing electrification of rural areas through the Rajiv Gandhi 
Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana.

Free supply of power 
493. SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN: Will the Minister of POWER be 
pleased to state what steps are being taken by Government to desist the State 
Governments from free supply of power to any user including farmers? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE). As 
per the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003 the State Electricity Regulatory 
Commissions (SERCs) have the powers to fix tariff for sale of electricity to 
consumers including farmers. 
Section 65 of the Act provides that if the State Government requires the 
grant of any subsidy to any consumer or class of consumers in the tariff 
determined by the State Commission, the State Government shall pay to the 
concerned utility/licensee the full amount required to compensate the grant of 
subsidy. 
Government of India has notified Tariff Policy under the provisions-of the 
Act. The Policy states that extent of subsidy for different categories of consumers 
can be decided by the State Government keeping in view various relevant aspects. 
But provision of free electricity is not desirable as it encourages wasteful 
consumption of electricity besides, in most cases, lowering of water table in turn 
creating avoidable problem of water shortages for irrigation and drinking water 
for later generations.

state:

required money? 
THE MINISTER OF POWER (SHRI SUSHILKUMAR SHINDE): (a) to 
(c) National Electricity Policy envisa ges "Power for all by 2012". To meet

To meet this objective, the need for investment of about Rs. 9,00,000 crore in

envisaged and the need for attracting substantial private investment has been

National Chemical Laboratory, Pune 
503. SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN: Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether National Chemical Laboratory, Pune has developed a filter 
for the elimination of both bacteria and viruses; 
133 

RAJYA SAB HA [23 February, 2006] 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps being taken by Government to promote the new 
technology and making it available on reduced prices? 
THE MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL 
SIBAL): (a) and (b) Yes Sir. The Nati onal Chemical Laboratory, Pune has 
developed an ultrafiltration (UF) membrane made from a polymer which does 
not allow bacteria and viruses such as (Hepatitis 'A & 'E') to pass through. 
Since the filtration device based on UF membrane enables operation at tap 
water pressure with an overhead tank, it has been found to be very useful for 
potable water filters. 
The UF membrane technology developed by NCL, has been transferred to an 
entrepreneur, M/s. Membrane Filters (India) Pvt. Ltd., Pune to develop water filters. 
A manufacturing facility has been set-up for spirally wound membrane and 
assembly for water filters of different models and sizes, including a hand pump 
operated system capable of delivering over 125 litres/hour of potable water. 
The household module is 30 cm long with 6.5 cm diameter; while a longer 
one (1 m long with the same diameter) is suitable for community applications. 
The water filtration rate for 30 cm module is 1 lit/min. and 3 lit/min. at 1 bar 
pressure for community module. Average life of the membrane is estimated to 
be 3 years and cost of filtration is reported to be 5-7 paise per litre of pure 
water. 
The invention has been patented in India and abroad. 
(c) Department of Science and Technology through its rural technology 
division is promoting the installation of these membrane filters in rural areas at a 
subsidized cost, it is also being done under the project sponsored by Department 
of Drinking Water Supply under the Rajiv Gandhi National Drinking Water 
Mission. The Government has also provided forty units of water filter to 
NGOs in different parts of the country for their dissemination.

Maritime Development Programme in Orissa 
506. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have launched the Maritime Development 
Programme in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the details of the projects that are proposed to be taken up in Orissa 
coastline under the above scheme? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a) and (b) The Government has 
formulated the National Maritime Development Programme under which a total 
of 387 projects covering entire gamut of activities in the Maritime Sector are 
planned to be taken up for implementation over a period upto 2024-25. Total 
investment envisaged in the Programme is Rs. 1,00,339 crores. Out of these, 
276 projects involving a total investment of Rs. 55,804 crores to be taken up 
for implementation upto 2011-12 relate 
139 

RAJYA SABHA [23 February, 2006] 
to major ports and the balance 111 projects involving a total investment of Rs. 
44,535 crores pertain to Merchant Shipping and Inland Water Transport. The 
activities covered under the Programme include deepening of port channels, 
construction/upgradation of berths and terminals, modernization of port 
equipment, inprovement in road and rail connectivity to major ports, 
improvement in backup facilities in major ports, tonnage acquisition maritime 
training and coastal shipping. 
(c) A total of 28 projects pertaining to Paradip Port, the.only major port 
in Orissa, have been identified for inclusion in the Programme. Total investment 
involved in these projects is Rs. 2403.67 crores. Major projects include deepening 
of the port channel to handle 1,25,000 DWT vessels (Phase I), deepening of the 
port channel to handle 1,85,000 DWT vessels (Phase II), construction of deep 
draft iron ore berth, construction of berths for berths for clean cargo, 
development of a container terminal, mechanized coking coal handling 
facilities, four-laning of roads from Chandikhole to Paradip Port NH-5Aand 
Cuttack to Paradip SH-12 through National Highways Authority of India and 
enhancement of rail connectivity between Haridaspur and Paradip Port through 
the Railways.

Revival of domestic shipping industry 
512. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether, of late many shipping companies in India are moving out of 
the country due to a high-tax shipping regime comprising of 12 different 
taxes/levies; 
144 

[23 February, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) whether the problems of the domestic shipping industry has been 
compounded by the removal of restriction on using a foreign-flag vessel in 
India, denying a level playing field for the domestic shipping industry; and 
(c) whether the removal of Tonnage Tax Act has shown any 
favourable impact on the revival of the domestic shipping industry? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a) Not yet Sir. However, the Indian 
shipping industry is burdened with a variety of taxes which is denying level 
playing field to the Indian industry vis-a-vis their international competitors. 
(b) The restrictions on using foreign flag vessel in India have not been 
removed. In order to ease congestion in container movement at Jawaharlal 
Nehru Port Trust (JNPT)/Mumbai Port Trust, two relaxations of six months each 
were given under Section 407(3) of Merchant Shipping Act, 1958, in January, 2005 
and August, 2005, for movement of containers by foreign ships between 
JNPT/Mumbai Port Trust to any other port in India or wee versa. Foreign flag 
vessels are allowed to be chartered in by an Indian entity, only in the absence of 
availability of matching Indian Flag vessels. 
(c) There is no proposal in the Government for removal of Tonnage Tax 
In fact Government has introduced the tonnage tax for shipping industry from 
the year 2004-05. There has been improvement in tonnage since its introduction 
and the gross tonnage of shipping industry has increased by 25.11% during 
the last two years.

Water Management Training Agreement with France 
526. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY: Will the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether France has agreed to help India to set up a training centre 
for water services and technologies in order to tackle with the problem of poor 
water management relating to drinking water; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) by when pilot plants would be set up; 
(d) whether Government propose to take the help of other countries in this 
regard; 
(e) if so, the details thereof; and 
(f) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIAJAY MAKEN): (a Yes, Sir. 
(b) The Indo-French Joint Working Group on Urban Development 
decided in its meeting held in October, 2004 that Training Centre for Water 
Services and Technologies (TCWST) should be set up in India Subsequently, 
International Office of Water (IOW), France conducted a feasibility study for 
setting up of the Training Centre in June/July, 2005. The draft report of the 
study has been prepared. During the next meeting of the Indo-French Joint 
Working Group on Urban Development held on 19.1.06, it was decided that a 
'Realisation Study' for setting up of Training Centre should be carried out to 
finalise issues like structure of the organization, financial viability of the 
project and substainability of the institute. Once, the 'Realisation Study' is 
completed the process of setting up the Training Centre would be initiated. 
(c) The pilot plants would form part of the Training Centre and would be 
set up simultaneously. 
(d) to (f) The Training Centre is proposed to be set up with bilateral and/or 
technical assistance under the Indo-French Financial Protocol.

Details of schemes being implemented for development and promotion of 
sports in the country 
SCHEME OF INCENTIVES FOR PROMOTION OF SPORTS 
ACTIVITIES 
The scheme will have following components: 
(a) Pension to Meritorious Sports Persons—To provide incentive as well as 
an added measure of financial security to sportspersons in recognition 
of their outstanding performance in identified international 
competitions. 
186 

[23 February, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) Rural Sports Programme—To provide incentive to promote sports and to 
generate sports consciousness and mass participation in sports in the 
rural areas. 
(c) Promotion of Sports and Games in School—To provide incentives to 
promote sports and games among the school children. 
(d) Sports Scholarships—To recognize the achievements of young sports 
persons and their outstanding performance at the National, State, College 
and University levels. 
(e) National Sports Development Fund—To apply the moneys of the 
National Sports Development Fund for promotion of sports in 
general and specific sports disciplines and individuals sportspersons in 
particular for achieving excellence at the national and international level. 
SCHEME RELATING TO AWARDS 
The Scheme has the following thr ee components under which awards 
are given to outstanding sportspersons for winning medals in international 
sports events: 
(a) Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award—The scheme was launched in the 
year 1991-92 for honouring the outstanding sportspersons in a year for 
his/her achievements in sports. 
(b) Special Awards to Winners in International Sports Events and their 
Coaches—The scheme was introduced in the year 1986 to encourage 
and motivate outstanding sportspersons for even higher achievement and 
to attract the younger generation to take sports as a career. 
(c) Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (MAK A) Trophy—Inte r-University 
Tournaments are an integral and important part of games and sports in 
universities and colleges. The top overall performing university in the 
Inter-University Tournaments is given the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad 
(MAKA) Trophy, which is a rolling trophy. A small replica of the 
MAKA Trophy is also awarded for retention by the University. In 
addition, the university also gets a cash prize of Rs. 2.00 lakhs. The 
second and third best universities also gets cash awards amounting to 
Rs.1.00 lakh and Rs 0.50 lakh respectively. 
187 

RAJYASABHA [23 February, 2006] 
SCHEME RELATING TO TALENT SEARCH AND TRAINING  
The scheme aims at providing a pack age of assistance to the promising 
sportspersons in the sports disciplines, based on the chances of getting medals in the 
coming Olympics and other international sports events and providing assistance to 
supporting personnel such as the sports scientists, coaches, referees, sports specialists, 
etc. with a view to provide scientific back up and other support to the 
promising sportspersons. 
ASSISTANCE TO NATIONAL SPORTS FEDERATIONS 
Financial assistance is given to recognized National Sports Federations 
(NSFs) for sending their teams abroad for training and participation in 
international tournaments, holding international tournaments in India, conducting 
National Championships and also for procuring equipment. Assistance is also extended 
through the Sports Authority of India for organizing coaching camps for preparing 
national teams and for engaging the services of foreign coaches. Limited secretarial 
assistance is also provided to NSFs byway of reimbursement of salary of Joint/Assistant 
Secretaries of the Federations. 
SCHEME OF INSTITUTIONS 
SAI has two Academic Wings namely (i) SAI Netaji Subhash National Institute of 
Sports (NS NIS), Patiala (Punjab) which prepares sportspersons in the field of 
coaching and also conducts research and development in sports; and (ii) SAI 
Lakshmibai National College of Physical Education (LNCPE), Thiruvananthapuram 
(Kerala), which offers Graduate and Masters Degrees in Physical Education and also 
conducts Research and Development in Physical Education. 
SCHEME OF STATE SPORTS ACADEMY 
The Government of India have a Scheme for giving grants to sponsors of State 
Sports Academies. The main objective of the Scheme is to select the best available talent 
in sports in the age group 10—13 years, as well as top performers in State/National 
competitions in the age group 10—18 years, and to prepare and groom them over the 
years for winning medals for the country at the international level. 
188 

[23 February, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
The Scheme envisages setting up State Sports Academies as a co-operative 
venture with joint funding by the Central Government, State Government/UT 
Administration and a Sponsor. The financial assistance to the Academy in respect of 
capital-non-recurring cost with an upper cap of Rs. 8.30 crore is to be shared between 
the Sponsor, the Central Government and the State Government in the ratio of 51 25:24. 
In addition, recurring cost up to Rs. 17.00 lakhs per annum or 25% of actual 
expenditure, whichever is less, is payable for a period of three years by the 
Government of India. 
SCHEME FOR DOPE TEST 
The scheme for dope test was launched in the Tenth Five Year Plan with the 
following objectives:—to have an International Olympic Committee accredited Dope 
Control Centre Hi India; to maintain quality control system as required by 
International standard, i.e. ISO: 17025; to educate athletes, coaches and other 
supporting personnel about the harmful effects of dope; to test and develop the 
rationale for drug free sports and national anti-doping policy; to conduct in-competition 
and out-of-competition dope tests on sportspersons; to promote research and training, 
and above all, to harmonize the dope related regulations in tune with the World Anti-
Doping code and the rules and regulations frames by the World Anti Doping Agency 
from time to time. 
NATIONAL SPORTS CHAMPIONSHIP FOR WOMEN 
The scheme started in 1975, aims at promoting sports amongst women. Under 
the scheme, national level competitions are preceded by holding of lower level 
competitions (Block, District & State level) for which States/UTs are provided financial 
assistance as per norms. The scheme is implemented through the Sports Authority of 
India. 
NATIONAL WELFARE FUND FOR SPORTSPERSONS 
The National Welfare Fund for sportspersons was set up in March, 1982 with a 
view to assist outstanding sportspersons of yesteryears, living in indigent circumstance who 
had won glory for the country in sports. Under the scheme, financial assistance is 
provided in the form of pension and lump-sum grant to the sportspersons as well their 
families. Monthly 
189 

RAJYA SABHA [23 February, 2006] 
pension up to Rs.2500/- is given to outstanding sportspersons whose monthly 
income is less than Rs.3000/- p.m. The fund is operated by a Committee with 
the Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports as the chairperson. 
BRIEF ON SPORTS AUTHORITY OF INDIA'S SPORTS 
PROMOTIONAL SCHEMES 
1. National Sports Talent Contest— The main concept of the scheme 
is to Play and Study in the same school scientific scouting of talent at 
optimum age essential for converting the genetically and physiologically 
gifted children into future medal hopes in various competitions at National 
and International level. The children in the age group of 8 to 14 are admitted 
under the Scheme. Presently there are 32 regular schools, 49 Navodaya 
Vidyalayas, 27 schools for Promotion of Indigenous Games and Martial Arts 
and 23 Akharas adopted under the scheme with strength of 2110 trainees. In 
addition to this 33 upcoming akharas have been provided equipment support. 
2. Army Boys Sports Company— With a view to utilize the 
disciplined atmosphere of Army and infrastructure available, Army Boys Sports 
Company Scheme was introduced in association with Army in which children 
are identified in the age group of 8 to 14 and admitted in the Scheme. The 
identified trainees are absorbed in the Army, once they finished their sporting 
career. At present there are 18 ABSC with strength of 780. The children 
admitted under the schemes are provided with boarding, lodging @ Rs.75/- per 
day for 300 days, Sports Kit @ Rs.2000/-p.a., Insurance cover @ Rs.150/- pa, 
Competition Exposure @Rs.2000/-p.a., Medical Expenses @Rs.300/-, 
Educational Expenses @ Rs. 1000/-p.a. One time grant of Rs. 2000/- to a New 
Trainee. The companies are provided annual grant of Rs. 50000/- for purchase 
of sports equipments and maintenance of play fields. 
3. SAI Training Centre —In order to groom the junior level sports 
persons in the age group of 14 to  21, with the assistance of State 
Governments, SAI Training Centres are established in which the State 
Government need to provide with all the infrastructure facilities. SAI is 
running the scheme by providing scientific training to the selected trainees. 
190 

[23 February, 2006] RAJYA SABHA 
Trainees are provided with boarding, lodging @ Rs.100/- per head per day for 
10 months, Sports Kit of Rs.4000/- pa., Accidental insurance Rs. 150/- p.a., 
Competition Exposure Rs.3000/- p.a., Educational Expenses Rs.,1000/- p.a., 
Medical Expenses Rs. 300/- pa. At present, the training is imparted to 5790 
trainees in 28 disciplines in 57 SAI Training Centres all over the country. 
4. Special Area Games—The schemes of Special Area Games aims to 
scout and nurture the natural talent for modern competitive sports and games from 
inaccessible tribal, rural and coastal ar eas of the country. The children are 
admitted in the age group of 14 to 21 . There are 16 SAG Centres with 1390 
trainees all over the country. The trainees admitted under the scheme are provided 
with boarding, lodging @ Rs. 100/- per head per day for 10 months, Sports Kit 
of Rs. 4000/- p.a., Accidental Insurance Rs. 150/- p.a., Competition 
Exposures Rs. 3000/- p.a., Educational Expenses Rs. 1000/- p.a., Medical 
Expenses Rs. 300/- p.a. At present, the training is imparted in 22 disciplines. 
5. Centre of Excellence—In order to provide second and third tier to the 
National Team, it was decided to start the Centre of Excellence Scheme to 
train those sportspersons who have shown performance at senior national level 
competitions. The trainees in the age group of 21 and above are admitted. 
Admission is also given to junior level sports persons who are in the verge of 
entering into the senior level and has potential to become international 
sportspersons. At present there are 10 Centres of Excellence, 8 at Regional 
Centres of SAI and one each at LNCPE, Trivandrum and STC, Lucknow with 
strength of 404. The training is imparted in 16 disciplines. The trainees are 
provided with boarding, lodging @ Rs. 100/- per head per day for 10 months, 
Sports Kit of Rs. 3000/- p.a., Accidental Insurance Rs. 150/- p.a., Competition 
Exposure Rs. 3000/- p.a., Medical Expenses Rs. 500/- p.a.

Till 31.3.2005, the Ministry was operating a Centrally Sponsored Sports 
Infrastructure Scheme under which Central Assistance was provided for 
creation of Sports Infrastructure subject  to the receipt of viable proposals. 
The Government had decided to transfer the Sports Infrastructure Schemes to 
State Sector w.e.f. 1.4.2005 and accordingly no funds have been allocated in the 
BE 2005-06 for Sports Infrastructure Schemes. All State Governments were 
informed of this in February, 2005. Thus, fresh proposals for sports infrastructure 
projects have to be funded by State Governments from their own resources. 
However, the Planning Commission has confirmed that funds to the extent of 
the committed liabilities will be provided for on-going approved sports 
infrastructure projects during the Tenth Plan.
